prompt_en: Make a photorealistic environmental portrait as a layered photographic colour study, showing the reference-informed woman at the storm entrance of a small seaside observatory at blue hour. The supplied photograph guides visible face and hair appearance: her short dark bob, wispy forehead fringe, softly rounded jaw, dark eyes and natural lip shape stay recognizable at this different angle. Here she is an evening maintenance technician, and she is finishing a careful piece of maintenance before the outer storm door can close. A narrow rubber weather strip lies partly seated along the open doorway, with its last loose end visibly raised. She kneels with her left knee on a folded pad and her right boot planted on the dry inner floor; her connected right forearm reaches down and her right fingertips press that loose strip end into the threshold channel, while her left palm rests flat on the adjacent stone. Her concentrated gaze follows the short remaining gap, her face slightly lifted enough to see her features, lips softly parted, the small intimacy of absorbed work carrying her appeal. Rain beads cling to the outer glass and a dark wet track stops beyond the strip, making the practical reason for this task legible. She wears an ivory rib-knit long-sleeved top with fine charcoal horizontal stripes under a matte charcoal canvas work apron; one small muted brick-red woven tab on the apron repeats the hue of a compact brick-red painted-steel toolbox beside the pad. The stripes belong to the fabric, and the red belongs to these two small object surfaces. The broad neutral-gray limestone floor and neutral plaster doorway form the quiet dominant field, the ivory clothing is a secondary light area, and the small red pair is a sparing accent. A warm-white desk lamp visible on a shelf at the left of the inner room illuminates the near stone, her nearer cheek, fingers and ivory sleeve. Blue dusk daylight enters through the glass storm porch beyond and to the right, cooling the far floor, the other side of the doorjamb and the rim of her dark hair. The same continuous neutral limestone crosses the threshold: its near section receives creamy warm illumination and its far section receives blue illumination, with a readable transition tied to the doorway and source directions. The intrinsically gray wall, ivory knit, charcoal fabric and red objects keep their separate local colours within those casts. A small satin-metal latch at the doorway catches a narrow pale reflection, distinct from the matte apron, ribbed knit and softly mottled stone. Photograph from waist height inside the warm room in a three-quarter view, including her crown, both working hands, kneeling support, toolbox, full threshold and cool porch window in one horizontal frame. Her face and fingertips lead attention; the strip and two-room colour boundary explain the moment next. Use natural perspective and enough depth to read the near lamp and far window, restrained saturation, neutral camera colour rendering, and midtone detail that lets the source-dependent casts read as light on receiving surfaces.
